questions.q: Which statement correctly describes eukaryotic cells?
opts: Their genetic material is enclosed in a nucleus
Their genetic material is a single loop
They are always smaller than bacteria
They never have a cell membrane
ex: Correct. "Eukaryote" means "true nucleus": the DNA is enclosed inside a nucleus.
A single DNA loop is what prokaryotes have.
Eukaryotic cells are larger than bacteria, not smaller.
All cells have a cell membrane.

questions.q: Which structure do bacterial cells have that animal cells do not?
ex: Bacteria do not have a nucleus. Animal cells do.
Animal cells have mitochondria. The specification does not list them for bacteria.
Correct. Bacteria have a cell wall; animal cells do not.
Both bacteria and animal cells have a cell membrane, so it is not a difference.

questions.q: Where is the genetic material in a bacterial cell?
opts: In a single loop of DNA in the cytoplasm
ex: Bacteria have no nucleus.
Correct. The main DNA is a single loop free in the cytoplasm. There may also be small rings called plasmids.
The cell wall surrounds the cell and does not hold the DNA.
Mitochondria are not part of the specification for bacterial cells.

questions.q: A student writes: "Prokaryotic cells are smaller." Which addition would make this a better comparison?
ex: Age has nothing to do with it.
Correct. A comparison names both cell types in the same sentence.
Prokaryotes do have a cell membrane.
Prokaryotes have no nucleus.

questions.q: A cell is 100 µm across. A bacterium is 1 µm across. About how many times larger is the cell?
ex: Correct. 100 µm ÷ 1 µm = 100, which is two orders of magnitude.
That would need a 1000 µm cell.
That would need a 10 000 µm cell.

questions.q: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration?
ex: The nucleus holds the DNA and controls the cell.
Ribosomes make proteins.
Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis, not respiration.
Correct. Respiration releases energy in the mitochondria.

questions.q: Why do muscle cells contain many mitochondria?
opts: To release a lot of energy for contraction
ex: Proteins are made at ribosomes.
Correct. Mitochondria release energy by respiration, and muscle contraction needs a lot of it.
Absorbing light is the job of chloroplasts.
The nucleus controls the cell, not the other way round.

questions.q: Which part of a bacterial cell can carry genes for antibiotic resistance and be passed to other bacteria?
ex: Correct. Plasmids are small rings of DNA that carry extra genes and can transfer between bacteria.
The cell wall does not carry genes.
Ribosomes make proteins.
The cytoplasm is where reactions happen; it does not carry genes between cells.

questions.q: Which is found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
ex: Plant and animal cells both have mitochondria.
Both have a cell membrane.
Both have ribosomes.
Correct. Plant cells often have a permanent vacuole filled with cell sap.

questions.q: What is the function of the cellulose cell wall?
opts: To control what enters and leaves the cell
ex: That is the job of the cell membrane.
Correct. The wall strengthens the cell.
Energy is released in mitochondria.
Light is absorbed by chlorophyll in chloroplasts.

questions.q: Root hair cells have long extensions. What is the benefit?
opts: They give a large surface area for absorbing water and ions
ex: Correct. A larger surface area means more water and mineral ions can be absorbed.
Root cells have no chloroplasts, so they cannot photosynthesise.
Nerve impulses are carried by nerve cells.
Storing sugars is not the role of root hair cells.

questions.q: A sperm cell has a tail. How does this help it do its job?
opts: It lets the sperm swim to the egg
ex: Food is not stored in the tail.
Correct. The tail allows the sperm to swim towards the egg.
The DNA is in the head (the nucleus).
Strength is not the tail's function.

questions.q: What is the correct description of differentiation?
opts: A cell dividing into two identical cells
The process by which a cell becomes specialised for a job
ex: That is cell division.
Correct. Differentiation is the process; the result is a specialised cell.
Cell death is a different process.
Absorbing water is not differentiation.

questions.q: Which statement about differentiation is correct?
opts: Animal cells differentiate throughout life, plant cells only early
Both differentiate only in early life
Most animal cells differentiate early, but many plant cells can differentiate throughout life
Neither differentiates after birth or germination
ex: This is the wrong way round.
Many plant cells can still differentiate later.
Correct. This is a key difference between animals and plants.
Many plant cells keep the ability to differentiate.

questions.q: Why did electron microscopes let scientists see more sub-cellular structures than light microscopes?
opts: They have higher magnification and higher resolution
ex: The magnification is higher, not lower.
Light microscopes use light; electron microscopes use electrons. "Less light" does not explain it.
Correct. Higher magnification and higher resolving power show finer detail.
Cost is not the reason.

questions.q: An image is 12 mm long. The magnification is ×400. What is the real length?
ex: That is 12 × 400. Real size = image ÷ magnification.
12 ÷ 40 would give 0.3. The magnification is 400.
That is 400 ÷ 12.

questions.q: A cell is 50 µm long in real life. It is drawn at ×200 magnification. How long is the drawing?
ex: That divides when it should multiply.
Wrong factor: 50 × 200 = 10 000 µm, not 250.
Correct. Image = real × magnification = 50 × 200 = 10 000 µm = 10 mm.
Check the units: 10 000 µm is 10 mm, not 10 µm.

questions.q: One bacterium divides every 20 minutes. How many bacteria after 1 hour, with enough nutrients?
ex: That counts the divisions, not the population.
Doubling three times gives 8, not 6.
Correct. 60 min = 3 divisions and 2³ = 8.
That would be one new bacterium per minute.

questions.q: Why is an inoculating loop passed through a flame before being used?
opts: To kill microorganisms already on the loop
ex: Warming the bacteria is not the aim.
Correct. Sterilising kills unwanted microorganisms so only the intended culture is transferred.
Flaming does not dry the agar.
Stickiness is irrelevant.

questions.q: Why are school cultures normally incubated at 25 °C rather than 37 °C?
opts: To reduce the chance of growing pathogens that thrive at body temperature
Because 25 °C is the fastest growth temperature
ex: Many bacteria can grow at 37 °C. That is the problem.
Correct. Human pathogens grow best near 37 °C, so a lower temperature is safer.
Agar does not melt at 30 °C.
Growth is usually faster at higher temperature, which is why 25 °C is a safety choice.

questions.q: A clear zone has a diameter of 14 mm. Which gives its area (to 3 s.f.)?
ex: That is the circumference (π × 14).
Correct. r = 7 mm, so π × 7² = 153.9, i.e. 154 mm².
That uses r = 14 mm. Halve the diameter first.
That is 14², not π r².

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a neutron?
ex: That is a proton.
That is an electron.
Correct. Neutrons are neutral.
No particle in the atom has +2.

questions.q: The atomic number of an atom is the number of…
ex: Neutrons are not counted in the atomic number.
Correct. The atomic number is the number of protons.
That is the mass number.
The number of shells is unrelated.

questions.q: Which statement describes isotopes of an element?
opts: Same number of neutrons, different protons
Same number of protons, different neutrons
Same mass number, different atomic number
ex: Changing the protons changes the element.
Correct. Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
That describes atoms of different elements with the same mass number.
Electron number differs in ions, not isotopes.

questions.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of ³⁵₁₇Cl?
ex: 17 is the number of protons.
Correct. 35 − 17 = 18.
35 is the mass number.
52 adds protons and mass number, which is meaningless.

questions.q: Where is most of the mass of an atom found?
ex: Electrons have very little mass.
Correct. Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus.
Mass is concentrated, not spread out.
Outer electrons have almost no mass.

questions.q: Copper has two isotopes: 69% copper-63 and 31% copper-65. What is its relative atomic mass (1 d.p.)?
ex: Correct. (69 × 63 + 31 × 65) ÷ 100 = 6362 ÷ 100 = 63.6, closer to 63 because that isotope is more abundant.
This is the simple mean of 63 and 65. It ignores the percentage abundances.
This only uses the more common isotope. The 31% of copper-65 pulls the average up a little.
This swaps the percentages, so it weights copper-65 as the more abundant isotope.

questions.q: What is the electronic structure of an atom of potassium (atomic number 19)?
ex: The third shell holds 8 electrons for the first 20 elements, so the 9th electron goes in a fourth shell.
Correct. Shells fill 2, then 8, then 8, with the last electron in a fourth shell.
Electrons fill inner shells first.
That adds up to 19 but fills in the wrong order.

questions.q: How many electrons are in the outer shell of an atom with electronic structure 2,8,7?
ex: 2 is the first shell.
Correct. The last number is the outer shell.
8 is the second shell.
17 is the total number of electrons.

questions.q: Which model described the atom as a ball of positive charge with electrons embedded in it?
ex: The nuclear model has a small central nucleus.
Correct. This is the plum pudding model.
Bohr placed electrons in shells.
The solid sphere model had no sub-atomic particles.

questions.q: In the alpha scattering experiment, most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil. What does this show?
opts: The atom is mostly empty space
The atom is a solid ball
ex: Correct. Most of the atom is empty space, with a tiny dense nucleus.
If it were solid, more would be deflected or blocked.
Gold atoms have electrons.
Alpha particles are positively charged.

questions.q: Electric current is best defined as…
opts: the energy transferred by a circuit
the rate of flow of charge
the push that makes charge flow
how much a component resists flow
ex: That is closer to power.
Correct. Current is the rate of flow of charge.
That is potential difference.
That is resistance.

questions.q: A current of 3 A flows for 20 s. How much charge flows?
ex: That divides 3 by 20 the wrong way.
That divides 20 by 3. The equation is Q = I t.
That adds the numbers.
Correct. Q = 3 × 20 = 60 C.

questions.q: A 9 V battery is connected across a 3 Ω resistor. What current flows?
ex: That multiplies V and R; current = V ÷ R.
Correct. I = 9 ÷ 3 = 3 A.
That is R ÷ V.
That subtracts, which is not in the equation.

questions.q: A resistor has a current of 0.2 A when the potential difference is 5 V. What is its resistance?
ex: That is 5 × 0.2.
That is 0.2 ÷ 5. Resistance = V ÷ I.
Correct. R = 5 ÷ 0.2 = 25 Ω.
That subtracts, which is not in the equation.

questions.q: What does the I–V graph of an ohmic conductor at constant temperature look like?
opts: A straight line through the origin
ex: That is not ohmic behaviour.
Correct. Current is directly proportional to potential difference.
A horizontal line would mean current does not change.
That describes some non-ohmic components.

questions.q: Why does the resistance of a filament lamp increase as the current increases?
opts: The lamp gets brighter, which adds charge
ex: The wire does not lengthen noticeably.
Correct. A hotter filament has more resistance, so the graph curves.
The potential difference does not fall.
Brightness does not add charge.

questions.q: Which component allows current to flow in only one direction?
ex: A thermistor changes resistance with temperature.
Correct. A diode conducts one way only.
An LDR changes with light.
A fixed resistor conducts both ways.

questions.q: As the temperature of a thermistor increases, its resistance…
ex: That is the pattern for a metal wire.
Correct. A thermistor's resistance falls as it gets hotter.
It changes, which is why it is useful in sensors.
That describes a diode in reverse.

questions.q: An LDR is placed in bright light. What happens to its resistance?
ex: That is what happens in the dark.
Correct. Resistance falls as light intensity rises.
It changes with light.
Resistance has no direction.
